doc: Mastodon / fediverse content, read-only: one post, its poll, a conversation, a feed and an account. Renders from plain Mastodon-shaped data — no network of its own and no clock. Which server it reads is CONFIGURATION, not code: the two origins its views name and the name it writes in prose are variables a host binds at load, so one build serves mastodon.social, hachyderm.io or any instance there is.

config.name: mediaOrigin
config.doc: Where this instance serves avatars, profile headers and attachment previews. ONE origin draws a whole federated timeline, because a server proxies what it federates: a remote account's avatar and a remote post's attachment are both re-served here, under /cache/. The views name it; the records only supply the path under it.

config.name: webOrigin
config.doc: Where this instance's pages are: a profile, a hashtag, and the permalink of a post that is local to it. Remote profiles are here too, because the server renders them at its own address — a remote POST is not, and stays selectable text.

config.name: instanceName
config.doc: The server this reader belongs to, as a person writes it. Prose only — the full @user@server handle, a link's tooltip, and the visible text of a permalink. Never an origin: a text variable cannot reach a view, which is what keeps it from becoming one.

components.name: Scope
components.doc: What the answer beside it does NOT cover: a cap that stopped it, a page nobody read, an instance that only sees what it federates. Not an error and not a warning — the sentence that turns a count into a claim a reader can check.

messageDocs.name: summary
messageDocs.doc: Everything this scope discloses, as one line — the card's tooltip.

messageDocs.name: hasAny
messageDocs.doc: Whether there is anything to disclose at all. A scope with nothing to say draws nothing.

messageDocs.name: truncatedLabel
messageDocs.doc: What stopped the answer early, spelled out.

messageDocs.name: moreLabel
messageDocs.doc: That another page existed and was not read.

fields.name: truncated
fields.doc: A cap stopped this before the data ran out. The field that matters most: it is the difference between "there is no more" and "I stopped looking".

fields.name: truncatedBy
fields.doc: What stopped it, in the caller's own words — `limit`, `depth`.

fields.name: more
fields.doc: There is another page, and nobody asked for it.

fields.name: notes
fields.doc: What this answer does not cover, one sentence each. Free text because the reasons are not a closed set: an instance that only federates what somebody on it follows, and a filter the server applied, are both true and neither is a boolean.

inits.name: a federated timeline
inits.argsJson: {"more": true, "notes": ["this instance only holds posts it has federated, which is what somebody here follows", "posts from servers it has defederated are not in the set at all"]}
inits.doc: The disclosure a fediverse card most needs and had no field for: a timeline is what THIS instance has seen, which is not the network.

inits.name: a conversation that was cut short
inits.argsJson: {"truncated": true, "truncatedBy": "depth", "notes": ["replies on servers this one has not federated are not shown"]}
inits.doc: What a thread leaves out, which is where a card looks most complete and is least so.

components.name: Status
components.doc: One fediverse post: who wrote it, what it says (with its hashtags, mentions and links found and checked), what it carries and how it was received. Also the row a Thread, a Timeline and a Profile are made of.

messageDocs.name: toggleFavourite
messageDocs.doc: Favourite this post, or take the star back. Optimistic: the count moves here and a `favourited` / `unfavourited` bubble says so.

messageDocs.name: toggleBoost
messageDocs.doc: Boost this post, or undo the boost. Refused for a followers-only or direct post, which Mastodon does not let anybody boost.

messageDocs.name: toggleBookmark
messageDocs.doc: Save this post to read later, or take it out.

messageDocs.name: toggleReveal
messageDocs.doc: Open the content warning, or close it again. Not announced: unlike a favourite there is nothing for a host to write.

messageDocs.name: reply
messageDocs.doc: Answer this post. There is no composer here, so it is only the announcement — a `replyTo` bubble carrying the id.

messageDocs.name: toggleFold
messageDocs.doc: Fold the replies under this post away, or bring them back. Only a row inside a thread has any.

messageDocs.name: favourited
messageDocs.doc: This reader favourited the post; carries its id.

messageDocs.name: unfavourited
messageDocs.doc: This reader took a favourite back; carries its id.

messageDocs.name: boosted
messageDocs.doc: This reader boosted the post; carries its id.

messageDocs.name: unboosted
messageDocs.doc: This reader undid a boost; carries its id.

messageDocs.name: bookmarked
messageDocs.doc: This reader saved the post; carries its id.

messageDocs.name: unbookmarked
messageDocs.doc: This reader unsaved the post; carries its id.

messageDocs.name: replyTo
messageDocs.doc: This reader wants to answer the post; carries its id. Whoever holds the component is what opens a composer.

messageDocs.name: folded
messageDocs.doc: This row folded its replies away; carries its id. The row keeps the flag; the thread above is what knows which posts stop rendering because of it.

messageDocs.name: unfolded
messageDocs.doc: This row brought its replies back; carries its id.

messageDocs.name: voted
messageDocs.doc: A poll under this post was voted in. It passes straight through — only a component with a network can post a vote.

messageDocs.name: unvoted
messageDocs.doc: A poll vote under this post was taken back.

messageDocs.name: summary
messageDocs.doc: The author and the three counts, as one sentence.

messageDocs.name: revealLabel
messageDocs.doc: What the content-warning button says right now.

messageDocs.name: boostTitle
messageDocs.doc: What the boost button will do, or why it will not.

messageDocs.name: foldTitle
messageDocs.doc: What the fold button will do, spelled out — its label is a glyph.

messageDocs.name: owned
messageDocs.doc: Set by whoever builds a row; it draws smaller and sits inside their column.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: The status id on the server it was read from, which the permalink is built out of.

fields.name: url
fields.doc: The status's canonical url, as the record carries it. For a post from another server this is all there is — no view can name that origin — so it stays text.

fields.name: acct
fields.doc: The author's full fediverse handle: `alice` on this server, `alice@other.test` from anywhere else. Whether it carries an `@` is what decides whether there is a local permalink.

fields.name: displayName
fields.doc: The author's display name; the handle stands in when it is empty.

fields.name: avatar
fields.doc: The author's picture, as the full url the record carries. Drawn when it is on files.mastodon.social — the origin the view names, which a remote account's picture is on too, because the server proxies what it federates.

fields.name: content
fields.doc: What the post says, as PLAIN text. Mastodon's own `content` is HTML and an untrusted bundle may not emit markup, so the hashtags, mentions and links are found in the text and checked against the two lists below.

fields.name: spoilerText
fields.doc: The content warning. Non-empty hides the body behind a Show more button.

fields.name: createdAt
fields.doc: When it was posted, as an ISO 8601 stamp.

fields.name: visibility
fields.doc: public | unlisted | private | direct. It picks the glyph beside the stamp, and the last two cannot be boosted.

fields.name: tags
fields.doc: The hashtags the SERVER resolved, without their `#`. A `#run` in the text that is not here stays plain text: only the server knows which of them are real.

fields.name: mentions
fields.doc: The accounts the server resolved, as full `acct`s. Same rule as the hashtags, and the carried spelling is what the link uses.

fields.name: media
fields.doc: Attached pictures as { description, previewUrl, url, type }. The preview is drawn when it is on files.mastodon.social; one without a picture is its description on a chip, and one WITH a description gets Mastodon's ALT badge.

fields.name: poll
fields.doc: The poll, as { options, votesCount, votersCount, expiresAt, expired, multiple, voted, ownVotes }. Empty options means there is no poll; anything else becomes a child Poll.

fields.name: repliesCount
fields.doc: How many replies the record came with.

fields.name: reblogsCount
fields.doc: How many boosts the record came with.

fields.name: favouritesCount
fields.doc: How many favourites the record came with.

fields.name: favourited
fields.doc: Whether this reader has favourited it, counted on top of favouritesCount.

fields.name: reblogged
fields.doc: Whether this reader has boosted it, counted on top of reblogsCount.

fields.name: bookmarked
fields.doc: Whether this reader has saved it. Mastodon shows no count for this one, and neither does this.

fields.name: revealed
fields.doc: Whether this reader opened the content warning.

fields.name: boostedBy
fields.doc: Who boosted this into the timeline it is being read in; empty when nobody did.

fields.name: pinned
fields.doc: Whether the author pinned it to their profile.

fields.name: edited
fields.doc: Whether it has been edited since it was posted.

fields.name: depth
fields.doc: How deep in a reply tree this post sits; 0 stands on its own. Drawn as that many rails, since an untrusted view has no style attribute to indent with.

fields.name: focus
fields.doc: Whether this is the post its thread is about; marks the card.

fields.name: foldable
fields.doc: How many replies sit under this one in the thread that built it. 0 hides the fold button.

fields.name: folded
fields.doc: Whether this reader folded those replies away.

fields.name: owned
fields.doc: Whether this post is a row inside a larger surface — a thread, a feed — rather than standing on its own. A row draws smaller and borderless, inside the column that owns it.

components.name: Poll
components.doc: The poll under a post: its options, what this reader picked, and the share each one has. Its bar is a <progress>, because an untrusted view has no style attribute to make a width out of.

messageDocs.name: vote
messageDocs.doc: Pick the option at this index, or unpick it. One choice replaces the previous one unless the poll is multiple; a closed poll refuses.

messageDocs.name: voted
messageDocs.doc: This reader picked an option; carries the status id and the index.

messageDocs.name: unvoted
messageDocs.doc: This reader took a pick back; carries the status id and the index.

messageDocs.name: summary
messageDocs.doc: The poll's shape and how many votes are in, as one sentence.

fields.name: statusId
fields.doc: The post this poll belongs to, so a vote can say what it voted on. A poll has no way to find that out for itself.

fields.name: options
fields.doc: The options in order, each { title, votesCount }.

fields.name: votesCount
fields.doc: Votes cast, as the record had them. This reader's own are counted on top rather than added in.

fields.name: votersCount
fields.doc: How many people voted — fewer than votesCount when the poll is multiple choice.

fields.name: expiresAt
fields.doc: When the poll closes, as an ISO 8601 stamp.

fields.name: expired
fields.doc: Whether it has closed. A closed poll shows its results and refuses a vote.

fields.name: multiple
fields.doc: Whether more than one option may be picked.

fields.name: voted
fields.doc: Whether this reader had already voted when the record arrived.

fields.name: ownVotes
fields.doc: Which options this reader picked, by index.

inits.name: open
inits.argsJson: {"statusId": "117090000000000001", "options": [{"title": "yes, if the view names the origin", "votesCount": 41}, {"title": "no, an image is a GET it chose", "votesCount": 17}, {"title": "only from the host's own origin", "votesCount": 8}], "votesCount": 66, "votersCount": 66, "expiresAt": "2026-08-15T09:41:00Z", "expired": false, "multiple": false, "voted": false, "ownVotes": []}
inits.doc: A poll still open and not yet voted in: options as buttons, no numbers, which is what Mastodon shows before you answer.

inits.name: closed
inits.doc: A closed poll with a pick already in it: every share drawn, the leading option marked, and no vote left to cast.

components.name: Thread
components.doc: A conversation: the posts of a reply tree, flattened and indented by depth, each rendered as a Status of its own, with any subtree foldable.

messageDocs.name: folded
messageDocs.doc: A row folded its replies away — the thread is what knows which rows those are, so it drops them and stops the bubble here.

messageDocs.name: unfolded
messageDocs.doc: A row brought its replies back.

messageDocs.name: favourited
messageDocs.doc: A row was favourited. The row keeps the flag; the thread lets the bubble travel on, because only a component above can write to a server.

messageDocs.name: unfavourited
messageDocs.doc: A row's favourite was taken back.

messageDocs.name: boosted
messageDocs.doc: A row was boosted.

messageDocs.name: unboosted
messageDocs.doc: A row's boost was undone.

messageDocs.name: summary
messageDocs.doc: How many posts there are, and how many are folded away.

messageDocs.name: firstPage
messageDocs.doc: Jump to the first page.

messageDocs.name: prevPage
messageDocs.doc: Show the previous page.

messageDocs.name: nextPage
messageDocs.doc: Show the next page.

messageDocs.name: lastPage
messageDocs.doc: Jump to the last page.

messageDocs.name: paged
messageDocs.doc: Whether this list is long enough to be shown a page at a time — what the footer is drawn on. A short one draws no pager at all.

messageDocs.name: atFirst
messageDocs.doc: Whether this is the first page, which is what disables the two buttons that go back.

messageDocs.name: atLast
messageDocs.doc: Whether this is the last page, which is what disables the two that go on.

messageDocs.name: pageLabel
messageDocs.doc: Which page of how many, as the footer writes it.

messageDocs.name: rangeLabel
messageDocs.doc: Which rows this page holds — “26–50 of 340” — because a page number does not say.

fields.name: posts
fields.doc: The conversation in reading order, each post { id, url, acct, displayName, avatar, content, spoilerText, createdAt, visibility, tags, mentions, media, poll, repliesCount, reblogsCount, favouritesCount, depth } — depth being how deep in the reply tree it sits.

fields.name: focus
fields.doc: The id of the post the thread is about; that row is marked. Empty for none. Writing it rebuilds the rows.

fields.name: scope
fields.doc: What this conversation does not show — the depth the caller asked for, and the replies this instance has never federated. Same record shape a Timeline's scope takes.

fields.name: pageSize
fields.doc: How many posts a page holds. A card breaks a list into pages only once it is longer than a hundred rows, because a pager over forty of them costs a reader a click and buys nothing; asking for a size here asks for the window whatever the length, and starts at the first page.

components.name: Timeline

messageDocs.name: clearQuery

messageDocs.name: mediaLabel

fields.doc: The posts, newest first, in the same shape a Thread's take; each becomes a Status of its own, standing on its own (no depth, nothing to fold).

fields.name: query
fields.doc: What is in the search box. The filter chooses among rows that are already built, so nothing a reader did to a row is lost by typing.

fields.name: mediaOnly
fields.doc: Whether the column is showing only posts with pictures.

fields.name: scope
fields.doc: What this page does not cover. Written as a plain record — the keys are the Scope component's own field names — and drawn only when there is something to disclose.

fields.name: pageSize
fields.doc: How many posts a page holds. A card breaks a list into pages only once it is longer than a hundred rows, because a pager over forty of them costs a reader a click and buys nothing; asking for a size here asks for the window whatever the length, and starts at the first page.

components.name: Profile
components.doc: One account: who it is, what it says about itself, its four columns, the labelled links under its bio, and its recent posts.

messageDocs.name: toggleFollow
messageDocs.doc: Follow this account, or unfollow it. Optimistic, and announced as a bubble.

messageDocs.name: followed
messageDocs.doc: This reader followed the account; carries its acct.

messageDocs.name: unfollowed
messageDocs.doc: This reader unfollowed the account; carries its acct.

messageDocs.name: summary
messageDocs.doc: The account and its counts, as one sentence.

messageDocs.name: followLabel
messageDocs.doc: What the follow button says right now — a locked account asks rather than follows.

messageDocs.name: favourited
messageDocs.doc: A post in the feed was favourited; the profile lets the bubble travel on.

messageDocs.name: boosted
messageDocs.doc: A post in the feed was boosted.

messageDocs.name: firstPage
messageDocs.doc: Jump to the first page.

messageDocs.name: prevPage
messageDocs.doc: Show the previous page.

messageDocs.name: nextPage
messageDocs.doc: Show the next page.

messageDocs.name: lastPage
messageDocs.doc: Jump to the last page.

messageDocs.name: paged
messageDocs.doc: Whether this list is long enough to be shown a page at a time — what the footer is drawn on. A short one draws no pager at all.

messageDocs.name: atFirst
messageDocs.doc: Whether this is the first page, which is what disables the two buttons that go back.

messageDocs.name: atLast
messageDocs.doc: Whether this is the last page, which is what disables the two that go on.

messageDocs.name: pageLabel
messageDocs.doc: Which page of how many, as the footer writes it.

messageDocs.name: rangeLabel
messageDocs.doc: Which rows this page holds — “26–50 of 340” — because a page number does not say.

fields.name: displayName
fields.doc: The account's display name; the handle stands in when it is empty.

fields.name: acct
fields.doc: The account's handle. A local one is a bare username and the view writes the server back on, because a fediverse handle without its server is half an address.

fields.name: note
fields.doc: The bio, as plain text for the same reason a post's body is.

fields.name: avatar
fields.doc: The account's picture, as the full url the record carries. Drawn when it is on files.mastodon.social; the initials show through when it is not.

fields.name: header
fields.doc: The strip behind the picture, same rule as the avatar, and a flat band of base-200 when there is none.

fields.name: followersCount
fields.doc: How many accounts follow it.

fields.name: followingCount
fields.doc: How many accounts it follows.

fields.name: statusesCount
fields.doc: How many posts it has written.

fields.name: createdAt
fields.doc: When the account was created; the profile shows its year under Joined.

fields.name: bot
fields.doc: Whether the account says it is automated; Mastodon puts a BOT badge on it.

fields.name: locked
fields.doc: Whether it approves its followers by hand, which turns Follow into Request follow.

fields.name: following
fields.doc: Whether this reader follows it, counted on top of followersCount.

fields.name: fields
fields.doc: The labelled rows under the bio, each { name, value, verified }. A value is usually a link on the ACCOUNT's own origin, so it is shown the way a posted link is: shortened text, whole url in the tooltip, no href. The check is the server saying the link pointed back.

fields.name: posts
fields.doc: Its recent posts, in the same shape a Thread's take; each becomes a Status of its own.

fields.name: pageSize
fields.doc: How many posts a page holds. A card breaks a list into pages only once it is longer than a hundred rows, because a pager over forty of them costs a reader a click and buys nothing; asking for a size here asks for the window whatever the length, and starts at the first page.
